_comment: China Desk — the existing China Mil Watch corpus and The PLA Watch archive.
This manifest describes the sources the pipeline ALREADY collects. It was
written to match production exactly, not to propose changes: every slug,
display_name and base_url here is byte-identical to the seed data in
storage/schema.sql, so syncing this manifest into the database cannot
rename or re-point an existing source.
public_status is 'legacy' because this desk is already published under its
own brand and must keep behaving exactly as it does today.

institutions.name_original: 中央军事委员会政治工作部
institutions.notes: Publisher of PLA Daily and its English portal.

institutions.name_original: 中华人民共和国国防部

sources.notes: Supplies roughly 87% of the corpus. Authoritative for how the PLA describes itself; Tier B because it is service media rather than a directive-issuing body.

Tier A as the ministry's own authorized public position. Cadence measured 2026-08-09 from the source's own listings (28 distinct publish dates across three months), never from our collection, which is the thing under test. The source stayed live throughout the 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-17 gap: the 2026-08-17 investigation traced the apparent silence to our own cross-source canonical selection, which discarded MOD copies in favour of PLA Daily reprints, plus exact-target-date discovery that could not see backdated items. Both are fixed. Remains active and Tier A; silence threshold stays 21 days; recovery of the articles missed during the gap is tracked separately and has not been performed. Do not treat as inert.

Adapter is a documented stub: the listing is JavaScript/API-rendered and returns stale 2020-era HTML to requests-based clients. Has contributed zero rows for the life of the project. Kept enabled so the health report shows it as not_implemented rather than hiding it.
State-linked rather than official. Signals PLA messaging to foreign audiences; an officially tolerated nationalist line is not an authorized institutional position.
Official English-language mirror under the same institution as PLA Daily. Marked 'mirror' so its republications do not inflate institution-level message volume once cross-source clustering exists.
